title: Cost to Paint Kitchen Cabinets in 2026
description: Pro and DIY costs to paint kitchen cabinets in 2026, priced per door and per linear foot, plus paint amounts and quote checks.

takeaways: HomeGuide puts a pro job at $2,000 to $6,500 for an average kitchen, while Angi averages $942 because many of its jobs are smaller.
Doing it yourself costs $200 to $600 in paint and supplies for most kitchens, but plan on 30 to 60 hours of work.

body:
Painting your cabinets is the cheapest way to get a new kitchen without new boxes. HomeGuide's 2026 figures put a pro job at $2,000 to $6,500 for an average kitchen. Angi's 2026 data puts its typical job at $425 to $1,466, with an average of $942. Doing it yourself runs $200 to $600 in materials. The gap is kitchen size, and this guide shows you how to price yours by door count, drawer count, and linear feet.

## What it costs in 2026

Pros price this work per door, per linear foot, or per square foot. You only pay one way, so use the other two as a check on any quote.

| How pros charge | HomeGuide 2026 | Angi 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per door | $70 - $125 | $100 - $250 |
| Per drawer front | $30 - $110 | Priced with the door |
| Per linear foot | $30 - $70 | $30 - $60 |
| Per square foot | $3 - $15 | $3 - $10 |
| Per cabinet | $120 - $190 | Not listed |

| Kitchen size | HomeGuide total | Angi total |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small, 70 to 100 sq ft of floor | $1,000 - $3,500 | $900 - $1,500 for 8 to 12 cabinets |
| Average, 100 to 200 sq ft of floor | $2,000 - $6,500 | $1,500 - $2,800 for 13 to 20 cabinets |
| Large, over 200 sq ft of floor | $5,000 - $10,000 | $2,800 - $5,000 or more for 21 to 35 cabinets |

Why do the sources land so far apart? Angi averages many small and partial jobs, such as one run of uppers. HomeGuide totals assume a full kitchen, sprayed, with prep and cleanup in the price. Labor is 80 to 85 percent of a pro bill on HomeGuide, and 70 to 80 percent on Angi. HomeGuide breaks a pro bill into $400 to $1,000 for materials and paint, and $1,600 to $5,500 for labor. Paint itself is $20 to $70 per gallon, and primer is $35 to $50 per gallon.

## Worked example: a kitchen with 20 doors and 8 drawer fronts

Say your kitchen has 20 doors, 8 drawer fronts, and about 30 linear ft of cabinet frontage, base run, wall run, and island combined.

Step 1: Work out the painted area.

- Doors: each door is 15 in wide by 30 in tall. That is 450 sq in, or 3.13 sq ft per side. You paint both sides, so 6.25 sq ft per door. 20 doors x 6.25 sq ft = 125 sq ft.
- Drawer fronts: each front is 24 in by 7 in, or 168 sq in, or 1.17 sq ft for the front and edges. 8 fronts x 1.17 sq ft = 9 sq ft, rounded.
- Boxes and frames: face frames about 40 sq ft, two exposed sides about 16 sq ft, and the island back about 10 sq ft. Total 66 sq ft.
- Total painted surface: 125 + 9 + 66 = 200 sq ft.

Step 2: Turn area into paint. Use 400 sq ft per gallon per coat, the low end of the 400 to 500 sq ft Benjamin Moore lists for Advance cabinet paint.

- Primer, 1 coat: 200 sq ft / 400 = 0.5 gallons. Rounded up like a buyer, you buy 1 gallon of primer.
- Paint, 2 coats: 200 sq ft x 2 coats = 400 sq ft of coverage. 400 / 400 = 1.0 gallons. Add 10 percent for spray loss and touch-ups and you get 1.1 gallons. Rounded up, you buy 2 gallons of paint.

Our [primer calculator](/blog/primer-calculator/) runs the same math for walls, and our guide on [how many coats of paint](/blog/how-many-coats-of-paint/) explains why cabinets get two finish coats over primer.

Step 3: Price the DIY job from the HomeGuide supply list.

- Paint: 2 gallons x $60 = $120, inside the $20 to $70 range.
- Primer: 1 gallon x $45 = $45, inside the $35 to $50 range.
- Supplies: brushes $15, roller kit $20, patching compound $10, scraper $8, tape $10, sandpaper $5, drop cloth $10, degreaser $15. Total $93.
- DIY total: $120 + $45 + $93 = $258.

That is the low end of the $200 to $600 DIY range both sources give, because this kitchen needs no repairs. A sprayer rental adds $40 to $100 per day on HomeGuide.

Step 4: Check the pro price two ways.

- Per linear foot: 30 linear ft x $30 to $70 = $900 to $2,100.
- Per piece: 20 doors x $70 to $125 = $1,400 to $2,500. Plus 8 fronts x $30 to $110 = $240 to $880. Total $1,640 to $3,380, before boxes, masking, and cleanup.

A real quote here usually lands around $2,000 to $3,500, inside HomeGuide's average range. A quote under $1,000 for this count means prep has probably been cut.

## How to count and measure your cabinets

Count openings, not boxes. Tally every door, drawer front, and fixed panel that will get paint. Note doors with glass, lazy Susan corners, and raised detail. Painters charge more for those because each takes longer to sand and spray.

Measure the run in linear feet along the counter and wall cabinets. A standard door is close to 15 in by 30 in (38 x 76 cm), but tall pantry doors change the area fast.

Count both sides of every door. That is the mistake home counts make most often. The inside gets paint too, and it doubles the door area. Write the count down before you call anyone, so each quote prices the same job.

## What pushes the price up or down

Prep is the big one. Grease has to come off, gloss has to be sanded, and dents have to be filled before primer. Angi notes prep can account for up to half of a pro cost. Cabinets over a stove cost more than cabinets in a little-used kitchen.

Material matters. Solid wood takes standard primer well. MDF soaks up extra primer. Laminate and thermofoil need a bonding primer, and peeling thermofoil often cannot be saved by paint. Angi puts material-only costs at $200 to $400 for solid wood, $250 to $500 for MDF, and $300 to $600 for laminate.

Door style and color matter too. Slab and Shaker doors are fast. Raised panels and carved detail price at the top of the per door range. Dark cabinets going white often need a third finish coat. HomeGuide notes alkyd cabinet paints cost 15 to 20 percent more than standard latex, but level out smoother and cure harder.

Spraying gives the smoothest finish and costs $40 to $100 per linear foot on HomeGuide, because masking takes hours. Brush and roll costs less. Cabinets taller than 8 ft can add up to 10 percent. New hardware runs $6 to $60 per piece fitted, and repairs before painting run $120 to $600, both on HomeGuide. Price extras apart from the paint quote so you can drop them.

## DIY or hire a pro?

DIY saves the labor, which is most of the bill. It costs time instead. HomeGuide puts a 200 sq ft job at 30 to 60 hours of your work, spread over 3 to 5 days of drying gaps. Pros take 3 to 5 days too, but that is crew time, not your evenings.

Do it yourself if doors are flat or Shaker, boxes are solid, and you can give up the kitchen for a week. Number every door and hinge as you take it off. Clean, sand, prime, then paint boxes while doors dry flat on sawhorses. Keep coats thin. Thick coats run, and runs show every time light hits a door front.

Hire a pro for heavy detail, peeling thermofoil, water damage at the sink base, or a dark to light change you cannot afford to redo. If you paint the walls too, price that apart with our [paint calculator](/blog/paint-calculator/).

## How to get a fair quote and keep the cost down

Get three quotes from painters who do cabinets often, not just walls. Give each the same written count. Ask what paint and primer are in the price, how many coats, and if doors are sprayed off site or in your garage. Ask what the quote leaves out. Hardware, repairs, painting inside boxes, and cleanup are common leave-outs. Get the scope in writing, and never pay in full up front.

Save where it does not hurt the finish. Take off doors and hardware yourself and hand the pro clean cabinets. Pick a standard color in satin, which HomeGuide notes hides small flaws better than gloss. Keep current hardware if it works. Contractors can check their numbers with our [painting estimate calculator](/blog/painting-estimate-calculator/).

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint kitchen cabinets yourself?
Most DIY jobs cost $200 to $600 for paint, primer, and supplies, per Angi and HomeGuide. Our example came to $258 for 20 doors and 8 drawer fronts. A sprayer rental adds $40 to $100 per day.

### How long does it take to paint kitchen cabinets?
A pro crew takes 3 to 5 days on HomeGuide. A DIY job on 200 sq ft takes 30 to 60 hours, spread across drying time. Keep doors off heavy use for the first week while paint cures.

### How long do painted kitchen cabinets last?
HomeGuide puts a pro job at 8 to 15 years. Angi puts a full repaint at every 8 to 12 years. Edges you grab most chip first, so keep leftover paint for touch-ups.

### Is painting cheaper than refacing or replacing cabinets?
Yes. HomeGuide lists painting at $2,000 to $6,500, refacing at $5,000 to $13,000, and replacement at $4,500 to $15,000. Paint only makes sense if boxes are sound and the layout works.

### Do kitchen cabinets need primer before paint?
Yes, on almost every job. Primer makes paint stick, blocks tannin and grease stains, and cuts finish coats. Bare wood, stained wood, laminate, and dark to light changes all need a full primer coat.

### Can you paint laminate kitchen cabinets?
Yes, if the laminate is bonded tight. HomeGuide notes laminate needs sanding first, plus a bonding primer. If it is peeling or bubbling, paint will not hold and new doors are the better spend.
